Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency and observability story. Procurement asked me to start a simple MAP so we can get an internal view of milestones and the billing path for a private-offer (we plan to commit via the AWS private offer). Can you share a one-page mutual action plan that shows:

- Acceptance/eval checkpoints and the technical acceptance criteria
- Expected invoice/PO flow and who signs/receives invoices
- Legal review window and expected signature date
- Any prerequisites for production (VPC peering, KMS onboarding, audit logs)

We are targeting a go-live in June but procurement wants clear invoice milestone dates so our finance team can plan cashflow.

Asha Reddy

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a short Mutual Action Plan and a draft SOW to serve as the initial artifacts for procurement and legal. High-level summary below and action items.

Summary (one-paragraph):
We recommend a 6-week evaluation cadence culminating in a technical acceptance gate. Invoices are generated at milestone acceptance (50% on PO activation / 50% on production acceptance) unless Orion prefers monthly invoicing — happy to adapt. Private-offer flow (AWS) -> Redwood issues invoice to finance@orionhealth.com -> Orion issues PO/commit to AWS private-offer code path.

Proposed MAP milestones (dates are placeholders — please confirm):
- Week 0 (kickoff): MAP sign-off + AWS private-offer activation (we provide private-offer instructions)
- Week 1–3 (eval): Integration checks, prefix caching validation, latency baseline runbook
- Week 4 (staged acceptance): Technical acceptance review with logs and perf traces
- Week 5 (canary): Small production canary on dedicated capacity
- Week 6 (full acceptance): Production acceptance and invoice finalization

Action items for procurement:
1) Confirm preferred invoice cadence (milestone vs monthly) and billing contact (we suggest finance@orionhealth.com).
2) Share legal redline window (target 7 business days for SOW review).
3) Confirm whether KMS/HSM integration requires an approved vendor list.

Attachments:
- MPA_Orion_Health_2025-05-04.xlsx (Mutual Action Plan, checklist)
- SOW_Redwood_Orion_v1.2.pdf (Draft Statement of Work)

Evelyn — adding a technical acceptance checklist to the thread so procurement can see what we will validate. I dropped a short tech appendix into the MPA spreadsheet (tab "Tech Acceptance"). Key points:

- Latency acceptance: 95th percentile token-latency <= 350ms on benchmark prompt set (1000 queries)
- QA & fidelity check: Regression tests against the provided prompt set; maximum decline in quality metrics of 2% vs baseline
- KV cache priming: Confirm prefix cache warming procedure and tested hit rate >= 60% during canary
- Security: Audit logs + KMS access validated and sample logs shared during staged acceptance

Also noting dependencies: we need an AWS private-offer code (or the procurement contact to accept invoice path through their marketplace). For GCP/Azure we offer equivalent private SKU flows — if you decide to change cloud please flag ASAP.

Karthik Iyer
Sr Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Evelyn / Karthik — thanks for the clear MAP and tech acceptance appendix. Procurement reviewed and we have two requests before we sign-off on the MAP:

1) Invoice cadence: Orion prefers invoice issuance at PO activation and then monthly thereafter (we cannot do milestone final payments without finance approval). Please confirm Redwood can accommodate monthly invoices tied to commit usage with a final reconciliation invoice at acceptance.

2) Billing contact: Confirm that invoices will be sent to finance@orionhealth.com and that POs should reference code ORN-PO-21984.

Tom Li (CFO) has also asked for a projected invoice schedule for May–July to approve cashflow. We are still planning for a June go-live but need predictable monthly billing numbers.

— Asha on behalf of Procurement
